Link topologies containing multiple network PHYs attached to the same
net_device can be found when using a PHY as a media converter for use
with an SFP connector
column2: on which an SFP transceiver containing a PHY can

column1: be used.
With the current model
column2: the transceiver's PHY can't be used for

column1: operations such as cable testing
The reason being that most of the logic for these configuration
from either ethtool netlink or ioctls tend to use netdev->phydev
in multi-phy systems will reference the PHY closest to the MAC.
Introduce a numbering scheme allowing to enumerate PHY devices that
belong to any netdev
column2: which can in turn allow userspace to take more

column1: precise decisions with regard to each PHY's configuration.
The numbering is maintained per-netdev
The numbering works similarly to a netdevice's ifindex
identifiers that are only recycled once INT_MAX has been reached.
This prevents races that could occur between PHY listing and SFP
transceiver removal/insertion.
The identifiers are assigned at phy_attach time
depends on the netdevice the phy is attached to. The PHY index can be
re-used for PHYs that are persistent.
